content: After loading something with readModuleData, is it possible to have memory management takeover objects in the compacted region (e.g. via a deep copy), so we don't need to keep track of the region and to free it later?

Hi @Leni Aniva , could you say more about your use case for this (if you still have one a year later)? Deep copies and freeing compacted regions are not currently possible, but I have tried this in an experimental branch. There are no plans to support this currently, but if it'd be useful to you I could try extracting out a small library.

𝚠𝚘𝚓𝚌𝚒𝚎𝚌𝚑 𝚗𝚊𝚠𝚛𝚘𝚌𝚔𝚒 said:

Hi Leni Aniva , could you say more about your use case for this (if you still have one a year later)? Deep copies and freeing compacted regions are not currently possible, but I have tried this in an experimental branch. There are no plans to support this currently, but if it'd be useful to you I could try extracting out a small library.

My use case is distributed proof search. I want to send a proof state from one machine to another without having to keep track of the generation of new objects.

What kind of data is in your proof state? My current implementation only supports "first-order" data - nats, arrays, scalars, inductives, but no thunks/closures/promises/tasks.

What do you mean by 'generation of new objects'?

𝚠𝚘𝚓𝚌𝚒𝚎𝚌𝚑 𝚗𝚊𝚠𝚛𝚘𝚌𝚔𝚒 said:

What kind of data is in your proof state? My current implementation only supports "first-order" data - nats, arrays, scalars, inductives, but no thunks/closures/promises/tasks.

What do you mean by 'generation of new objects'?

The data I send across machines is the state of Elab.Term.TermElabM.

What I mean by generation of new objects, is that once a proof state exists on a machine, I may use it to generate additional proof states. If I am using compacted regions, these new states would contain pointers to the regions, so I have to keep track of every single proof state relying on a particular compacted region.

Elab.Term.State can include closures through MessageData. Copying closures might be fine, I just haven't thought about it.

What kind of benefit are you getting from using compacted regions as opposed to just loading a JSON or binary serialization of the state? Loading them is quite fast and uses disk-backed pages thanks to mmap, but if you need to deep-copy the whole thing afterwards you might not see as much of a win.

𝚠𝚘𝚓𝚌𝚒𝚎𝚌𝚑 𝚗𝚊𝚠𝚛𝚘𝚌𝚔𝚒 said:

Elab.Term.State can include closures through MessageData. Copying closures might be fine, I just haven't thought about it.

What kind of benefit are you getting from using compacted regions as opposed to just loading a JSON or binary serialization of the state? Loading them is quite fast and uses disk-backed pages thanks to mmap, but if you need to deep-copy the whole thing afterwards you might not see as much of a win.

the closures in MessageData could be removed
how do I serialize the state with json? is that a feature in Lean?

Snir Broshi said:

deriving ToJson
(docs#Lean.ToJson)

its not that simple.

import Lean
open Lean

deriving instance ToJson for Elab.Term.State

There are many structures inside Elab.Term.State that have no obvious json serializers
If I use ToJson I also need to measure how much data i need to transfer across machines when there are 1000s of metavariables in a proof

I am not seriously suggesting JSON - it seems unlikely to be efficient. I was mainly wondering why use compacted regions rather than a more standard serialization format. It sounds like the answer is ease of use - it's easier to use existing APIs than to write and maintain (de)serialization routines? Then the deep copy thing might be useful to you, modulo closure support.

𝚠𝚘𝚓𝚌𝚒𝚎𝚌𝚑 𝚗𝚊𝚠𝚛𝚘𝚌𝚔𝚒 said:

I am not seriously suggesting JSON - it seems unlikely to be efficient. I was mainly wondering why use compacted regions rather than a more standard serialization format. It sounds like the answer is ease of use - it's easier to use existing APIs than to write and maintain such a format? Then the deep copy thing might be useful to you, modulo closure support.

when I looked into serialization of Lean states, compacted regions seemed to be the only option. Have the options changed since I posted this question?
In terms of what's already out there with a single SomeFormat.saveToDisk call away, I don't believe so.
